You're Hitler's most trusted spy in Britain. You run twenty-seven secret agents. And not one of them exists.
It's 1941. You're a chicken farmer from Spain, and you hate the Nazis.
So you offer to spy for the British. They turn you down. Again and again.
So you go to the Germans instead, and tell them you're moving to London.
They hire you. But you go to Lisbon, and make everything up, with a tourist guide, a map, and old newsreels.
You've never even been to Britain. Your reports are full of mistakes. The Germans love them.
Then British codebreakers catch the Germans hunting a convoy that doesn't exist, and they come looking for you.
Now you work for London. Your fake spy ring grows to twenty-seven agents, and Germany pays every one of their salaries.
June 1944. Hours before D-Day, you warn Berlin that the Allies are landing in Normandy. Too late to matter. But now they trust you completely.
Three days later, you tell them Normandy is a trick. The real invasion is coming at Calais.
Hitler believes you. He keeps his armies waiting at Calais for weeks.
So Germany gives you the Iron Cross. And Britain makes you a member of the British Empire. Two medals, from both sides of the same war.
